tier_reason: The independent wasmi-benchmarks suite (benches/criterion startup group, runtimes/tinywasm/lib.rs, runtimes/wasmtime/lib.rs, plots in wasmi-labs/wasmi-benchmarks-plots data/amd-epyc-7763) compares Tinywasm with Wasmtime, Wasmer, WAMR and V8 on a named AMD EPYC 7763, and the plot's labels match every number in the record. Not A: no rustc or C compiler version is recorded anywhere (the CI workflows use dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable, no rust-toolchain file), and the plots do not record which runtime versions or suite commit produced them; it is third-party for Tinywasm (run by the Wasmi author), hence B.

corrections.baseline: Wasmtime (Cranelift, Winch, Pulley), Wasmer (Cranelift, Singlepass) and WAMR fast-interpreter startup
corrections.claimed_speedup: Startup geomean on AMD EPYC 7763 relative to the per-case fastest runtime (lower is better): Tinywasm x37.19 versus Wasmtime (Pulley) x1777.72, Wasmtime (Cranelift) x1634.19, Wasmer (Cranelift) x1484.15, Wasmtime (Winch) x298.15, Wasmer (Singlepass) x162.12 and WAMR fast-interpreter x56.73; V8 is x33.27 and Wasmi v2 (lazy) x1.37. About 44x lower than Wasmtime Cranelift and 1.5x lower than WAMR (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: wasmi-benchmarks Cargo.toml [profile.bench]: lto = "fat", codegen-units = 1 (cargo criterion --bench criterion uses it; a separate [profile.ci] with thin LTO is not used by the workflows). Rust toolchain unpinned: no rust-toolchain file, CI workflows (.github/workflows/startup.yml, execute.yml) install dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable; C/C++ runtimes are built by their wrapper crates with the system compiler, version unstated. Tinywasm 0.10.0 is built with default features, without the nightly-tail-calls feature its README recommends for maximum performance.
corrections.caveats: The suite is maintained and run by the Wasmi author (Robbepop), so it is third-party for Tinywasm but run by a competitor. Ratios were read from the text labels of the rendered SVG; the plots repo records no runtime versions, toolchain or run date beyond its commit 'update AMD EPYC 7763 plots' (2026-08-25). The EPYC 7763 is the CPU of GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners, so the run probably came from the workflow_dispatch CI jobs on a shared VM, but the plots repo does not say so. The suite pins tinywasm 0.10.0 with default features (no nightly-tail-calls); tinywasm 0.11.0 shipped 2026-09-19. Startup-only win, as expected of an interpreter against compiling JITs, and no better than V8 (x33.27). Execution geomean on the same CPU (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi-benchmarks-plots/HEAD/data/amd-epyc-7763/lin-scale/geomean-execute.svg) is x40.50, slower than Wasmtime (Pulley) x27.92, WAMR x17.07, Wasm3 (eager) x16.51 and Wasmi v2 (eager) x12.40. The README itself points users wanting better performance to wasmi, wasm3, wazero, wasmer or wasmtime. In the independent Apple Silicon report (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebeckerspecialties/wasm-benchmark/HEAD/docs/runtime-comparison-2026-09-22.md, tinywasm 0.11.0 with nightly-tail-calls) tinywasm execution geomean is 3.20 vs Pulley 2.09 and WAMR 1.63 on M4 E-cores (2.98 vs 1.68 and 1.38 on A12), and it fails the legacy-exceptions modules. Last commit on the default branch main is 2026-09-22; the next branch was updated 2026-10-03.

notes: All six numbers in the record match the SVG labels (matched by y position: Tinywasm x37.19, Wasmtime Cranelift x1634.19, Wasmer Cranelift x1484.15, Winch x298.15, Singlepass x162.12, V8 x33.27); I added the Pulley and WAMR startup rows, since WAMR is a category baseline. Downgraded A to B: independent suite, but rustc and C compiler versions and the measured runtime versions are unrecorded (zenjpeg and cataggar/wamr precedents for unpinned toolchains). Shortcomings to record: startup-only win, slower than V8 on startup, slower than WAMR, Pulley and Wasm3 on execution, measured without its recommended nightly-tail-calls build, older 0.10.0 measured, Rust not C++. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0 OR MIT, 594 stars, not a fork, last main commit 2026-09-22 (corrected from the next branch's 2026-10-03).

tier_reason: First-party: wasmi-benchmarks and its plots repo are maintained and run by the Wasmi author (Robbepop). The harness (benches/criterion, runtimes/wasmi-v2/lib.rs), bench profile flags and the CPU (AMD EPYC 7763 in the plot title) are public and every number matches the plot, but no rustc or C compiler version is recorded (CI uses dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable, no rust-toolchain file) and the plots do not record which Wasmi v2 beta or baseline versions were measured, so not A; own suite with partial methodology is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Startup geomean on AMD EPYC 7763, relative to the per-case fastest runtime (lower is better): Wasmi v2 (lazy) x1.37 and Wasmi v1 (lazy) x1.56, versus Wasmtime (Pulley) x1777.72, Wasmtime (Cranelift) x1634.19, Wasmer (Cranelift) x1484.15, Wasmtime (Winch) x298.15, Wasmer (Singlepass) x162.12, WAMR fast-interpreter x56.73 and V8 x33.27; about 1,190x lower than Wasmtime Cranelift (derived from page data). Wasmi v2 with lazy translation but eager validation is x10.66 and eager Wasmi v2 is x38.88. Execution geomean on the same CPU: Wasmi v2 (eager) x12.40 versus WAMR fast-interpreter x17.07 (about 1.38x faster, derived from page data) and Wasmtime (Pulley) x27.92.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: wasmi-benchmarks Cargo.toml [profile.bench]: lto = "fat", codegen-units = 1 (cargo criterion --bench criterion uses it; a separate [profile.ci] with thin LTO is not used by the workflows). Rust toolchain unpinned: no rust-toolchain file, CI workflows (.github/workflows/startup.yml, execute.yml) install dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable; C/C++ runtimes are built by their wrapper crates with the system compiler, version unstated. At HEAD the suite pins wasmi 2.0.0-beta.10 (features auto-dispatch, validate), wasmtime 47.0.0, wasmer 7.2.0, v8 crate 150.1.0 and wamrx 0.3; versions used for the plotted run are not recorded.
corrections.caveats: First-party: the suite and the plots repo are maintained and run by the Wasmi author (Robbepop). Ratios were read from the text labels of the rendered SVG; the plots repo records no runtime versions, toolchain or run date beyond its commit 'update AMD EPYC 7763 plots' (2026-08-25), so the plotted Wasmi v2 is a pre-release beta (v2.0.0 was released 2026-09-01; the suite README links v2.0.0-beta.7 while Cargo.toml now pins 2.0.0-beta.10). The EPYC 7763 is the CPU of GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners, so the run probably came from the workflow_dispatch CI jobs on a shared VM, but the plots repo does not say so. Startup ratios are dominated by lazy modes: 'lazy' defers both compilation and validation of function bodies to first use, so x1.37 skips work that Cranelift, Winch and V8 do eagerly; lazy-translation with eager validation (x10.66) and eager mode (x38.88) are fairer compile-cost comparisons, and eager Wasmi v2 is slower than V8 (x33.27) on startup. Execution: Wasmi v2 (eager) x12.40 beats WAMR fast-interpreter x17.07, Wasm3 (eager) x16.51 and Wasmtime (Pulley) x27.92, but loses to Silverfir-nano's interpreter x9.02, Wasmtime (Cranelift) x1.15 and V8 x1.05. The Wasmi README itself shows no numbers. Rust, not C++.

notes: All numbers in the record match the SVG labels (matched by y position); I added the Pulley, WAMR and lazy-translation startup rows and the execution comparison against the WAMR and Pulley baselines. Downgraded A to C: Wasmi's own suite run by its author, rustc and C compiler versions unrecorded, and the measured Wasmi v2 beta and baseline versions not stated on the plots. Shortcomings to record: first-party benchmark, startup headline relies on lazy validation, eager startup slower than V8, execution far behind JITs and behind Silverfir-nano's interpreter, pre-release v2 beta measured, Rust not C++. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0 OR MIT, 2.3k stars, not a fork or archived, last commit 2026-09-01 (Wasmi v2.0.0 release prep), active.
